<description>
This is split off from #36521 (and not included in #36895), as it's effectively an independent improvement.

This introduces a number of additional checks that are applied during transaction deserialization, which reduce various worst case deserialization time scenarios:
* Reject transactions with more txins or more txouts than can possibly fit in a block (applied always)
* Reject transactions with 0 txins or 0 txouts (applied in P2P code only; there are RPCs like `fundrawtransaction` that explicitly support transactions with 0 inputs)

This is a mild behavior change, as detecting these problems early causes them to be treated as deserialization errors, which in P2P logic cause messages to be ignored instead of peer disconnection.
</description>

A funding template can have outputs before the wallet picks any inputs. I’d check that those outputs survive a `TX_NO_WITNESS` round trip here.

```patch

--- a/src/test/transaction_tests.cpp
+++ b/src/test/transaction_tests.cpp
@@ -1482,2 +1482,10 @@ BOOST_AUTO_TEST_CASE(reject_empty)

+    // A legacy transaction with outputs but no inputs can be read for funding.
+    CMutableTransaction no_inputs;
+    no_inputs.vout.emplace_back(1, CScript{} << OP_TRUE);
+    const auto no_inputs_ser{DataStream{} << TX_NO_WITNESS(no_inputs)};
+    const auto unfunded{deser_tx(no_inputs_ser, TX_NO_WITNESS)};
```

[2026-11-25] rc:4697812447 inline on src/primitives/transaction.h by l0rinc (member) (edited 2026-11-25):
[quoted text omitted]

This also changes what RPC and kernel callers can inspect. A short release note with the two counts would help explain why a transaction that used to decode now fails.

Document transaction decoding changes for callers

```patch
diff --git a/doc/release-notes-36906.md b/doc/release-notes-36906.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000000..3fd3e5c8bd
--- /dev/null
+++ b/doc/release-notes-36906.md
@@ -0,0 +1,20 @@
+P2P and network changes
+-----------------------
+
+- The node ignores `tx`, `block`, `cmpctblock` and `blocktxn` messages that
+  contain a transaction with no inputs or no outputs, or with more inputs
+  or outputs than can fit in a block.
+
+Updated RPCs
+------------
+
+- RPC decoding now rejects a transaction declaring more than 24,390 inputs
+  or 111,111 outputs. Either count alone exceeds the block weight limit.
+  With `iswitness` omitted, `decoderawtransaction` can still return a
+  different transaction if the same bytes decode in legacy format.
+
+Low-level changes
+=================
+
+- The same count limits apply to `btck_transaction_create` and
+  `btck_block_create`, which return null on decode failure.
```

Preserve output-count parsing for zero-input transactions

```patch
diff --git a/src/primitives/transaction.h b/src/primitives/transaction.h
index a4be11ca43..88a3161099 100644
--- a/src/primitives/transaction.h
+++ b/src/primitives/transaction.h
@@ -241,5 +241,4 @@ void UnserializeTransaction(TxType& tx, Stream& s, const TransactionSerParams& p

-    // Read the number of outputs. In case of an empty vin, the byte read as the flags is the number of outputs (if the
-    // flags are not zero, there is witness data without inputs, which fails below).
-    auto num_outputs = (num_inputs == 0 && fAllowWitness) ? uint64_t{0} : ReadCompactSize(s);
+    // Read the number of outputs unless we already read the zero output count as the flags byte.
+    auto num_outputs = (num_inputs == 0 && fAllowWitness && flags == 0) ? uint64_t{0} : ReadCompactSize(s);
     if (num_outputs > MAX_BLOCK_WEIGHT / MIN_WEIGHT_PER_TXOUT) throw std::ios_base::failure("Too many transaction outputs");
```

[2026-11-25] rc:4698767540 inline on src/primitives/transaction.h by l0rinc (member) (edited 2026-11-25):
[quoted text omitted]

I’d find these minimum weights easier to check if the expressions named the fields. `Txid::size() + sizeof(COutPoint::n)` shows where the 36 comes from, and `GetSizeOfCompactSize(0)` gives the empty script’s length prefix in both cases.

Use the serialized field widths for the minimum transaction weights

```patch
diff --git a/src/primitives/transaction.h b/src/primitives/transaction.h
index a7136281a9..ade6989299 100644
--- a/src/primitives/transaction.h
+++ b/src/primitives/transaction.h
@@ -184,6 +184,6 @@ inline constexpr TransactionSerParams TX_NO_WITNESS{.allow_witness = false};

-/** The minimum weight of a transaction input: its prevout (36 bytes), an empty scriptSig (1), and its nSequence (4). */
-inline constexpr uint64_t MIN_WEIGHT_PER_TXIN{WITNESS_SCALE_FACTOR * (36 + 1 + 4)};
-/** The minimum weight of a transaction output: its nValue (8 bytes) and an empty scriptPubKey (1). */
-inline constexpr uint64_t MIN_WEIGHT_PER_TXOUT{WITNESS_SCALE_FACTOR * (8 + 1)};
+/** Minimum input weight with an empty scriptSig. */
+inline constexpr uint64_t MIN_WEIGHT_PER_TXIN{WITNESS_SCALE_FACTOR * (Txid::size() + sizeof(COutPoint::n) + GetSizeOfCompactSize(0) + sizeof(CTxIn::nSequence))};
+/** Minimum output weight with an empty scriptPubKey. */
+inline constexpr uint64_t MIN_WEIGHT_PER_TXOUT{WITNESS_SCALE_FACTOR * (sizeof(CTxOut::nValue) + GetSizeOfCompactSize(0))};

```
[2026-11-25] r:6061260754 review COMMENTED by l0rinc (member):
ACK 82cd7e742729bdfd5ea3be9c029c63ee9ad1f59d

I’m glad you dropped the weight accounting and stream state - I was uneasy about touching that much serialization code for this, and the two remaining checks are much easier to review. I also prefer `reserve` with `emplace_back` here, filling each entry just after construction seems cache-friendlier - and it was slightly faster when I timed block decoding locally.

I’d give the decoder some room above the block-derived counts so a transaction with one extra input still gets the usual validation error - to be on the safe side, since we only want to reject very obviously wrong entries.
I’d also find the minimum input weight easier to check if it used the field widths directly in place of `36 + 1 + 4`. The output bound could also be shared with `AccessByTxid`. If we keep the tight caps, I’d lean toward a release note for RPC and kernel callers. With limits that only catch obviously excessive counts, I’d skip it.

`UnserializeTransaction` is the part I’d be most careful about changing again: I need the same parsing order in #36548 and would like to share it if there’s a small extraction we’re comfortable with.
I’d also find `end of data` clearer than `Superfluous witness record` when [the outputs are cut off](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36906#discussion_r4697816420).
